body:
Gold is trading in the low-$4,400s this month, and that's exactly where both platforms have clustered their contracts. Kalshi's Aug 7 update noted gold moved higher to $4,411.70 that morning even after a disappointing July jobs report, and futures had opened near similar levels a few days later on Aug 10. That backdrop lines up with today's data: Kalshi's Aug 31 settle above ladder crosses roughly 50/50 around the $4,400 strike, and Polymarket's touch contracts show similar odds clustering near $4,450-$4,500.

The scanner surfaced exactly one cross-platform opportunity, and it's a good example of why these things usually aren't free money. It pairs a Polymarket YES, gold touches $4,700 in August contract (0.078) with a Kalshi NO, gold settles above $4,731.99 on Aug 31 contract (0.91). These aren't the same bet: Polymarket's is a touch contract that pays out if gold hits the level at any instant during the month, while Kalshi's is a settle contract that only checks the price once, at 5pm ET on Aug 31. The logic linking them holds in one direction (if Kalshi's NO loses, gold must have touched above $4,731.99, which would also trigger the lower $4,700 Polymarket threshold), but the net edge is just 0.63 cents per contract after fees, and the book only supports 100 contracts -- about 63 cents of total profit. That's noise, not an actionable mispricing.

Beyond that, it's a quiet day. No same-underlying, same-resolution mismatches showed up, and the rest of the board -- Kalshi's monthly and year-end strike ladders alongside Polymarket's weekly touch markets -- is pricing consistently with gold sitting in the $4,300-$4,450 range.
headline: Gold clusters near $4,400 as cross-platform gap shrinks to noise-level 63 cents
